The season in one number
3
Trophies for Georgia in fourteen days: the FIFA Youth League on May 14, the Cotton Bowl on May 17 and the league on May 27
The treble
Champions on 96 points · 29 wins, 9 draws, 4 defeats · 48 goals conceded, level with UCLA’s record
The season finale · Season 2 · No. 11

Georgia, three times

Georgia went top on April 8 and stayed there. On May 27 they won 10–1 at TCU to finish on 96 points, three clear of Michigan, and the title was theirs. They had already won two other trophies that month: the FIFA Youth League final, 3–1 against North Carolina on May 14, with Will Sands, Ronaldo Damus and Jose Villaseñor scoring, and the Cotton Bowl three days later, 4–3 against LSU, with a hat-trick from Harrison Robledo. No club in this league has won the title, the Youth League and a bowl in the same season before. Michigan won the Rose Bowl and finished second, Oklahoma won the Fiesta Bowl and missed the Youth League places by three points, and Duke beat Clemson on the last day and still went down. This edition has all of it, plus the season awards, lottery night for the Seattle draft and the first week of the U20 World Cup.

By the Touchline desk · read straight from the save on Tuesday, May 30, 2023 · all 462 league games and every final counted

96

Georgia’s points, the second-highest total in the league’s two seasons after UCLA’s 102 in 2021–22

48

Goals Georgia conceded in 42 league games, the same as UCLA’s record. Miami kept the most clean sheets, 20

188

Texas’s league goals, a record; the old one was Miami’s 170. Four clubs passed it: Texas, Miami (184), Michigan (180) and Oklahoma (176)

58

Goals in all competitions for both Ronaldo Damus and Milan Iloski, eight more than Folarin Balogun’s Season 1 record

How this edition was made. Every number is read from the save: the table and every league goal, the bowl and Youth League results with their scorers, the U20 World Cup results so far, abilities, hidden attributes and each player’s season totals. The awards are Touchline’s own and are judged on the whole season in all competitions; the league has not announced its awards yet.

Finals fortnight

May 2 to May 17 · the Youth League and the three bowls

Four finals in four days, and every one had a winner from the Sixteen. Georgia won two of them, Michigan and Oklahoma one each. North Carolina, LSU, Ohio State and Texas Tech each lost one.

The Youth League. Georgia beat UCLA 2–1 in the quarter-final on April 11, and their semi-final is not readable in the save. North Carolina beat Miami in the other semi on April 26; that score is not readable either. The final turned at the end. Will Sands scored on 12 minutes and it stayed 1–0 until the 90th, when Damus doubled the lead. Korshunov pulled one back for North Carolina, and Villaseñor, who is 16, made it 3–1 a minute later. Last year Michigan beat North Carolina 3–1 in the final; North Carolina have now lost two in a row, both by the same score.

Three days later, the Cotton Bowl. Robledo scored after one minute and again after five. LSU were level by the 31st minute through Juan Castilla and Oli Griffin, Villaseñor put Georgia back in front on 57, and Robledo completed his hat-trick on 73.

Touchline’s Season 2 awards

The whole season · all competitions · our votes, not the league’s

Twelve awards, judged on everything from August 13 to May 27. Where the numbers tied, the tie-break is written on the card. Last year Samuel Shashoua won Player of the Year; this year the winner is a Georgian.

Player of the Year
Juan Pablo Torres Georgia · 22 · Winger48 assists · 13 goals · grade 98.7

The best player on the best team, and the highest-graded player in the league for the fourth month running. He made 48 goals in all competitions, three short of Samuel Shashoua’s record, created 89 clear-cut chances (the most) and 373 key passes. He was Player of the Month in February and scored in the 10–1 at TCU that finished the league.

Also on the ballot: Ronaldo Damus (Georgia), 58 goals, grade 97.9; Matko Miljevic (Michigan), 25 goals and 40 assists, grade 95.9.

Golden Boot
Ronaldo Damus Georgia · 23 · Advanced Forward58 goals · 32 in the league

Damus and Milan Iloski both finished on 58 goals in all competitions, eight more than the old record. The tie goes to Damus on two counts: he scored his in 3,232 minutes to Iloski’s 3,325, and only 3 were penalties to Iloski’s 16. He also led the league outright, with 32. He scored in the Youth League final and four at TCU on the last day.

Iloski (LSU) 58; Jonathan David (Miami) 53; Folarin Balogun (Michigan) 44. League: Damus 32, Nicholas Gioacchini 31, Josh Sargent 30.

Playmaker of the Year
Paxton Pomykal UCLA · 23 · Shadow Striker41 assists · 378 key passes · 19 PoM

UCLA finished fifteenth, and their No. 10 was still the best creator in the league. Most key passes (378), the most player-of-the-match awards (19) and the best average rating of any regular, 8.13. He also scored 27. He is 23 and in the draft; the board has him ninth.

Miljevic 40 assists; Jonathan Perez (Miami) 34; Marcos López (Ohio State) 33; Miguel Ramírez (Miami) 32.

Golden Glove
Brady Scott Miami · 22 · Sweeper Keeper19 shutouts · 28 conceded

Scott and Georgia’s Tomás Romero both kept 19 clean sheets, two more than Matías Soria’s record. Scott conceded 28 in 3,152 minutes to Romero’s 29 in 3,240, and grades highest of any keeper (89.4). Miami kept 20 league clean sheets, the most in the league.

Romero (Georgia) 19; John Pulskamp (Texas Tech) and Antonio Carrera (Michigan) 17; Gabriel Słonina (Alabama) grade 85.2.

Defender of the Year
Kobi Henry Georgia · 19 · Ball-Playing Defendergrade 86.5 · 631 headers won · 10 goals

The top-graded centre back in the league at 19, at the heart of the defence that conceded 48. He won 631 headers, and of every regular averaging 7 or more over his last sixteen games, none had steadier match ratings (standard deviation 0.30). He is in the U.S. Under-20 squad in Indonesia.

Josh O’Brien (Miami), 19 goals from centre back; Owen Otasowie (Texas Tech) 81.1; Matt Nocita (North Carolina) 80.3.

Wing Back of the Year
Taylor Booth Texas Tech · 21 · Inverted Wing Back16 goals · 25 assists · grade 90.9

Booth was the wing back in last season’s All-American XI and won the halftime award. He scored 16, made 25 and created 79 clear-cut chances, the third-most of anyone, for a Texas Tech side that finished eighth and reached the Fiesta Bowl final.

Marcos López (Ohio State) 14 goals and 33 assists; Jonathan Gómez (Texas) 78.2; Logan Panchot (North Carolina) 75.7.

Young Player of the Year
Evan Rotundo Oklahoma · 18 · Shadow Striker27 goals · 32 assists · 7.84

The award is for players 19 and under. Rotundo, who is 18, had the most goal involvements of any teenager in the league (59), and the U.S. Under-20s picked him for the World Cup. Oklahoma finished sixth and won the Fiesta Bowl.

Kobi Henry (Georgia, 19); Gabriel Słonina (Alabama, 19); Jonathan Gómez (Texas, 19); George Johnson (Texas, 16) 30 goals.

George Johnson (Texas, 16) 30 goals and 12 assists; Michael Hayton (Ohio State, 17) 30; Will Ockford (Alabama, 17) 26.

Brown and UCLA’s Matt Spear (60 → 93) both added 33 points of ability between August and May, the most in the league. Brown is ahead on where he finished, at 107, and on what he did: 12 goals for Notre Dame at 17.

Brian Morley (USC) +30; Will Ockford, Taye Beckham and Jack Imperato +29; Jose Villaseñor and Michael Hayton +28.

Coach of the Year
Georgia96 points · three trophies

The Georgia head coach. The league title, the Youth League and the Cotton Bowl, with the best defence in the league and the most home points (56 of 63). By ability, Georgia had the strongest top eleven in the league, but only just: Texas were 0.4 behind.

Also considered: the Michigan head coach (second, the Rose Bowl) and the Alabama head coach (fifth, with the tenth-strongest eleven).

Overachievers
North Carolina7th · 14th-strongest eleven

North Carolina’s top eleven by ability was the third-weakest in the league, and they finished seventh and reached the Youth League final. Alabama (10th by ability, 5th) and Miami (7th, 4th) also finished well above their paper strength.

Underachievers: Washington (6th-strongest eleven, 13th), Oklahoma (3rd, 6th) and Texas Tech (5th, 8th).

Ages are on May 30. Grades are the Touchline Grade for the whole season (1,700 minutes to qualify). The league usually names its own winners in June; last year its Player of the Year was not ours.

Six games, one season

Feb 11Game of the Season: Michigan 3–4 Texas

Michigan led 3–1 after 16 minutes. Texas came back, and Federico Oliva scored the winner in the fourth minute of added time. It was Michigan’s only home defeat of the season, and Michigan finished three points behind Georgia.

May 17Final of the Season: LSU 3–4 Georgia

The Cotton Bowl final. Robledo scored twice in five minutes, LSU drew level, and Robledo won it with his third. Iloski scored in added time.

Jan 28Biggest win: Miami 17–0 Oregon

Wilson Harris scored six. The biggest league win Touchline has on file in either season.

Jan 15Best individual game: Josh Sargent, six

Six of Texas’s goals in the 15–1 against Duke. Wilson Harris matched it two weeks later; nobody scored more in a league game.

Mar 11The draw of the season: USC 6–6 LSU

LSU led 2–0 and 5–3, USC led 6–5, and Agustin Anello equalised in the 89th minute. The highest-scoring draw of the season.

Apr 8The day it turned

Alabama beat Michigan 4–0 in Tuscaloosa and Georgia beat Oregon 5–0. Georgia went top that evening and never left.

How it finished

The April odds, the three games that decided it, and the race

On April 29 Touchline’s 20,000 simulations gave Georgia a 93.2% chance of the title, and Georgia won it. The top-five call was harder: the sims had Oklahoma (79.6%) and Alabama (78.4%) ahead of Miami (55.7%). Miami and Alabama made it and Oklahoma did not.

Points after each game

The top four, games 1 to 42

Michigan were ahead at the halfway mark, 51 points from 21 games to Georgia’s and Oklahoma’s 45. Georgia took 51 from their last 21, Michigan 42.

The three most important games, and what happened

May 27Miami 5–2 TexasRanked the most important game left. Miami needed it for a Youth League place and scored three in the first 16 minutes. Texas still finished third, because Michigan won 1–0 at North Carolina and went second.
May 6Washington 1–3 MiamiRanked second. Miami won it; their final-day win then lifted them to fourth.
May 27Florida 4–1 OklahomaRanked third. Alabama lost 6–1 at LSU the same afternoon, so a win would have put Oklahoma fifth on goal difference. Florida, sixteenth of the Sixteen, won 4–1. Oklahoma, who had lost 5–3 at home to Alabama on May 6, finished sixth.

May

The last two league rounds · May 6 and May 27

Two league games in May, three weeks apart, with the finals in between. Seven of the Sixteen won both: Georgia, Michigan, Miami, Notre Dame, Florida State, LSU and UCLA. Oklahoma, USC and Washington lost both, and Oklahoma fell out of the top five.

12–2Georgia’s May aggregate

Two wins. Selmir Miscic and Harrison Robledo beat Florida 2–1 on May 6, and Damus scored four in the 10–1 at TCU.

12–0Notre Dame at Oregon

The biggest win of May, on May 6. Malick Sanogo scored four and Yunus Musah three.

10–0Florida State v Oregon

On the last day. Cole Bassett scored three. Oregon finished with 4 points and 290 goals against.

5–4Texas Tech v USC

Nine goals on the last day. Texas Tech were 4–2 down with 14 minutes left and scored three, the winner from Giovanni Reyna on 87.

Player of the month

May · all competitions · April 30 to May 27
Georgia · Advanced Forward · 16 years old

Jose Villaseñor

5Goals
2Assists
6Games
7.70Avg rating
3Trophies

The month of finals belonged to a 16-year-old. Villaseñor scored a hat-trick in the 11–0 against El Paso in the Cotton Bowl quarter-final on May 3, the goal that made it 3–1 in the Youth League final on May 14, and Georgia’s third in the 4–3 Cotton Bowl final on May 17. Ten days later Georgia were champions. Others in May had higher average ratings; nobody scored more goals that mattered.

He finished the season with 32 goals and 13 assists in all competitions, which is also why he is Touchline’s Freshman of the Year. His ability is 117, up 28 since August, and his potential is 139. He is in the draft class of 2029.

Lottery night

The 2023 envelope, opened · Draft 23, Seattle, Tuesday, June 20

On December 31 Touchline sealed a random number and published its fingerprint. The USLP season ended on May 11, so the envelope can be opened. The draft order is decided by that number alone, and anyone can check it.

The seed

210cbbe02963700d76da38f9830e6740f1c3511978b69b17fc1fd8d465f367ba

SHA-256 of the seed is b8ff4f572a81773f…, the fingerprint printed on December 31 and in every edition since. It matches.

The rules. 84 players in the class (the Sixteen’s players born on or before June 20, 2000), so 21 drafting clubs: the top 21 of the final USLP table, four picks each, four rounds, snake order. The USLP finished in two groups of fourteen, so the top group takes the first fourteen places and Houston, seventh in the bottom group, have the 21st and last drafting place. New York missed it by a point.

The result. Seattle win the lottery. The host city picks first, at its own draft, from fourth in the table. Inter Miami, fourteenth, have the second pick. LAFC, the USLP champions, pick eighth. Inter Miami gain the most (14th in the table, slot 2); Atlanta United drop the furthest (5th, slot 19). Tampa Bay, last in round one, have back-to-back picks at both turns: 21 and 22, 63 and 64.

The Brannigan Board · mock draft

Hal Brannigan’s final board · now in the real order

For the first time the mock uses the real draft order. The board itself barely moved in May: the top fourteen are in the same order, give or take a swap, and Pierre da Silva climbs from 21st to 18th. The method is unchanged: potential 40%, current ability 30% and Touchline Grade 30%, with a small penalty for a 22-year-old who stopped growing. Each club takes the best player left, and no club takes two players in the same role while a comparable one is on the board. In the table, a dash in the board column means the player had no April rank on file.

Class of 2022 · the season in the pros

USL Premier · all competitions · the redraft

A year ago Los Angeles took the first and last picks of the 2022 draft. A season later, 47 of the 67 have grown, the class is up 243 points of ability in all, and the class has started 1,989 games. If the clubs could do it again, Weston McKennie (165) would go first, ahead of Christian Pulisic, who was the first pick and is still at 161.

The season’s numbers

  • Top scorer: Samuel Shashoua (Colorado), 24, still. Matías Succar (Atlanta United) 21.
  • Most minutes: Mark McKenzie (Columbus), 4,696. Weston McKennie played 4,461 with the best average rating in the class among those with 1,500 minutes (7.44).
  • Biggest riser: Jay Nunez, +16, taken 46th. Brannigan graded him a C− a year ago.
  • Steals: Nico Ramos (pick 61, redraft 31) and Colin Shutler (55th, 38th, +10).
  • Reaches: Brandon Austin (29th, redraft 53, 283 minutes) and Marco Farfan (27th, 48th).
  • Never played: four of the 67: Marlon Fossey, Carlos Avilez, Paul Lewis and Alex Touche.

Redraft = current ability, with minutes as a small tie-break. Club is the one that drafted him. Figures are the save’s season totals for the graduates’ current clubs.

This month in history

May 2022

A year ago this month, from Touchline’s Season 1 files. Every trophy from last May has a new holder.

May 15, 2022North Carolina 1–3 Michigan

The Youth League final, in Viareggio. A year later North Carolina lost the final again, to Georgia, by the same score.

May 18, 2022Alabama 2–2 Georgia, 7–6 on penalties

The Cotton Bowl final went nine rounds into the shootout. This year Georgia won it, 4–3 against LSU, without needing one.

May 18, 2022Michigan 1–2 UCLA

The Rose Bowl final. Michigan went back this year and beat Ohio State 3–2.

May 18, 2022Miami 3–3 North Carolina, 4–2 on penalties

The Fiesta Bowl. This year Oklahoma won it, and Miami went out to Texas in the first round.

May 28, 2022UCLA, champions with 102

Fourteen points clear. A year later they finished fifteenth with 64.

May 30, 2022The first lottery

LAFC won it from first in the table. This year Seattle did, from fourth.

Touchline Confidential

Notes from around the league
  • Three trophies change hands. Georgia took the Saint Marys Ferry Bell from Florida on May 6 (2–1) and kept it in the Cotton Bowl semi-final. LSU took the Gulf Coast Gavel from Alabama in the Cotton Bowl quarter-final (4–1), Alabama’s since December 2021. Oklahoma took the Red River Rail Spike from Texas in the Fiesta Bowl semi-final (1–0), Texas’s since September 2021. Michigan kept the Rust Belt Lantern in the Rose Bowl final. The Almanac’s trophy room is updated.
  • The host picks first. Of the 21 clubs in the lottery, the one hosting the draft drew the first pick. Nobody chose it: the seed was sealed on December 31, and Seattle were announced as hosts in April.
  • Georgia’s bill. The champions lose Torres, Damus, Pellegrini and Siad Haji to the draft: the Player of the Year, the Golden Boot winner and 185 goal involvements between the first three.
  • Two scores the save will not give up. Texas beat Miami in the Fiesta Bowl quarter-final on May 2, and Ohio State beat Washington in the Rose Bowl semi-final on May 10. Both are in the save without a readable score.
  • Akron, best of the rest. Akron finished seventeenth with 27 points, eight wins and the best defence of the six schools outside the Sixteen, 172 conceded. Oregon won one game all season and conceded 290.
  • Garrett’s season. Ten games, three goals, five assists, two player-of-the-match awards, and three of the assists in May. He is fifteen.
  • The awards to come. The league names its own Player of the Year in June. Last year it picked Efraín Álvarez from sixteenth-placed Florida State; Touchline picked Samuel Shashoua.

The Almanac is updated to the end of the season

The last snapshot of Season 2, read straight from the save on May 30: every player page carries his final ability, tier and season totals, and the Season 2 table is final.

  • Season 2 closes with the champions, the bowls and the Youth League in the season pages.
  • The Odds Desk is replaced by the final table, with the April call beside it. The trophy room adds May’s meetings.
  • Recruiting rankings recomputed; the class of 2023 is now a draft class with a draft order.
  • New Timeline posts from Georgia’s treble, lottery night and the U20 World Cup. Four new tier cards.

Touchline

Touchline is fiction. It’s an in-universe sports desk for a Football Manager 2022 save. Every table, result, goal, minute, appearance, rating, ability figure and hidden attribute on this page was read directly from the save file on May 30, 2023, with every league game, final and U20 World Cup game to May 30 counted. Player statistics are all competitions unless a line says league. Head coaches are referred to by role only. Real players appear only through their on-pitch record and their attributes in the save. Club crests are Touchline’s own designs in each school’s colours, not official marks.

Touchline’s awards, Touchline Grades, the power rankings, the Team of the Month, the odds, the record book, the board and the mock draft are this desk’s own work, not figures the game produces. The lottery order comes from a seed sealed on December 31, 2022 and published as a fingerprint the same day. Season 1 records and history come from Touchline’s own Season 1 files.

No one is quoted in this edition. Real players appear only through their numbers.
